projects.name: 3.1.4.9 - GCF - Indonesia REDD+ Results Based Payment
projects.description:
The overall objective of this project is to contribute to the achievement of the NDC and STRANAS objectives of reducing GHG emissions from the forest sector, while aligning with the Indonesia Mid-Term National Development Plan 2019-2024 contributing to sustainable development and poverty alleviation.

Five priority policies have had a particularly key role, directly and indirectly, in Indonesia successfully reducing
GHG emissions from the LUCF sector: 
a) The moratorium on issuance of new concessions in primary forests and peatlands, legally protecting 66 million hectares of natural forests and peatlandsfrom planned deforestation activities, or downgrading in functional status (e.g. from conservation to production forests). Renewed by Presidential Instruction every two years since 2011, it was made permanent in August 2019.
b) Forest Management Units (FMUs) (Kesatuan Pengelolaan Hutan– KPH). In all provinces. FMUs are the basis for governing and managing all forest areas and functions at the local level based on forest 
management plans, and in close consultation and collaboration with all stakeholders, including local government, community groups, local industries or license holders. FMUs are designed to be part of 
provincial government and to manage forests for their functional purpose (i.e. production, protection and conservation) while contributing to subnational development and community wellbeing. 
c) Tenure Conflict Resolution and Social Forestry Programme. The overall objective of the social forestry programme is to adjudicate, demarcate and transfer 12.7 million hectares of degraded forest land to communities to reduce poverty among forest dependent people while reducing deforestation and forest degradation, improving land management and conserving forests and valuable ecosystem functions.
d) Peatland and mangrove restoration. The Peat and Mangrove Restoration Agency (BRGM), which scope was recently expanded to include mangroves, aims to restore 1.2 million hectares of peatland and 600,000 hectares of mangrove ecosystem in critical condition by 2025, on top of the 3.2 million hectares of peatland restored since 2016 across seven priority provinces .
e) Land and forest restoration targets in national planning: The National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) 2019-2024 includes an ambitious target of 190,500 ha for land and forest restoration

The project is organized around 2 main results and corresponding project outputs, with a third component dedicated to project management:
1. The government’s capacity to coordinate and implement REDD+ at national and subnational level is strengthened.
2. Decentralized sustainable forest governance is expanded and enhanced

An enhanced rice seed program is linked to the FFS (sub component 4.1)

projects.name: 01001918 Enabling Blue Innovation Solutions for ASEAN’s Blue Economic Growth
projects.description: The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders recognized the importance of the Blue Economy and committed to promoting it by engaging with relevant stakeholders. Under Indonesia's ASEAN Chairmanship in September 2023, ASEAN launched the 'ASEAN Blue Economy Framework' as a reference document for ongoing discussions and initiatives related to the blue economy. It aims to guide ASEAN's initiatives, promote regional integration and cooperation, and enhance the sustainable use of aquatic spaces. Promoting the blue economy and innovations is crucial for realizing the ASEAN Blue Economy Framework within the broader context of ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP). This also aligns with the interest to pursue rule-based economic prosperity in a free and open Indian-Pacific region. It supports prosperity in the region, cooperation, connectivity, and a rule-based international order. Immediate implementation of the ASEAN Blue Economy Framework is necessary to test the concept on the ground. This project will support the implementation of Blue Strategies #2 and #3, focusing on blue science, technology, innovation, and priority sectors. It includes components such as a blue innovation challenge, a blue incubation program, and blue business matchmaking, providing support and resources to innovators in the blue economy sector. At least 2,200 innovation proposals are requested from ASEAN Countries and Timor Leste. Of those, 60 are awarded, with the remaining receiving technical advice to improve their business models and learn about blue, SDGs, and impact investing. The selected innovation solutions will directly benefit at least 396,000 people, with 30 percent being women. These solutions will address marine plastic pollution, climate issues, sustainable tourism, and sustainable fisheries. At least 220 investors, including 30 percent women-owned businesses, will directly benefit from business matchmaking and learning about blue, SDGs, and impact investing. At least 176 government officials, with 30 percent being women, will directly benefit from incubation engagement and business matchmaking. This transformative initiative will not only foster innovation and collaboration in the blue economy but also promises a sustainable future by addressing critical challenges, empowering women, and directly impacting lives across ASEAN and Timor Leste.

projects.name: 1.1.1.1 - Support comprehensive social protection reforms (Extension to workers in the informal economy, unemployment, maternity and sickness benefits) through gender sensitive and rights based improved policy and legal frameworks, and enforcement and delivery mechanisms in Indonesia
projects.description:
There are a number of issues that need improvement in the area of social security. For example, an old-age individual saving account scheme (JHT) collects the largest contributions of BPJS Employment and plays an overlapping function with the incoming employment insurance (JKP) and the existing old-age pension (JP). The old-age pension legally excludes a large majority of workers (i.e. wage earners who work at micro-enterprises and non-wage earners) and offers inadequate benefits compared to the requirement of the ILO’s social security minimum standards, while means-tested old-age benefit narrowly targets extremely limited beneficiaries without linkage to the BPJS’s old-age pension. Moreover, adding maternity and sickness benefits to the existing range of benefits would attract working age populations to participate in the BPJS Employment schemes; and as a consequence, would contribute to the formalisation of the informal economy.

The ILO will focus on creating conditions to gradually build comprehensive sustainable social protection systems for all by enhancing the expansion of the system coverage to workers (both in formal and informal economy), with a particular focus on the creation or reinforcement of the employment insurance branch and improving its linkages with ALMPs, and increasing its effectiveness and efficiency. In Indonesia the project will conduct a series of policy research; and facilitate policy dialogues and capacity building based on knowledge and evidence produced through the research activities.
Expected  outcomes: 
More workers are covered by social security schemes, through gender sensitive and rights based improved policy and legal frameworks, and enforcement and delivery mechanisms in Indonesia.
Better understanding and increased awareness at the regional level on the importance of social protection, with a focus on Employment Insurance.

projects.name: 3.1.1.42 - 00107123 Accelerating Climate Change Adaptation Investment Planning to Enhance Resilience in Indonesia (NAP Readiness)
projects.description:
Indonesia has already begun integrating Climate Resilience Planning into development planning. Indonesia's National Adaptation Plan process is based on the National Action Plan for Climate Change Adaptation (RAN-API 2013 – 2025). However, RAN-API has been replaced by the Climate Resilience Development/CRD Policy (Pembangunan Berketahanan Iklim / PBI). The Ministry of National Development Planning/Bappenas launched the Climate Resilience Development Policy document to work towards the end goal of climate resilience. Presidential Regulation Number 18 Year 2020 has made PBI one of the National Priorities (PN) 6 in the 2020-2024 National Medium Term Development Plan (RPJMN). The PBI provides up-to-date information and data on climate projections, hazards, and impacts in Indonesia, identifying marine and coastal, water, agriculture, and health as priority sectors for adaptation action. 

The main objective of the NAP GCF project is to ensure effective coordination, implementation, and monitoring of the Climate Resilience Development. The project operates at national and sub-national levels, supporting the update of PBI and enhancing assessment and budgeting systems. Additionally, it includes capacity building and training activities for sub-national landscape-based adaptation planning in Wakatobi, an archipelagic island site. 

The proposed project's three outcomes are as follows: 
1. Climate Resilience Development Policy Action Plan updated and integrated into budgeting system. 
2. SIDIK enhanced at national level for NDC sectors identified in adaptation component of the NDC. 
3. Integrated risk assessment and landscape based, climate resilience planning and budgeting established in Wakatobi.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.1 - Strengthened institutional capacities in government agencies and other key national stakeholders to develop, improve, and implement coordinated policies/strategies/plans for increased resilience to climate change and disasters and reduced greenhouse gas emissions

projects.name: 4.1.1.20  UN Global Pulse Asia Pacific (Phase 1 and 2)
projects.description:
UN Global Pulse serves as the United Nations Secretary-General's flagship innovation initiative, established in 2009 to harness the power of big data and technology for sustainable development. Functioning as the UN's innovation laboratory, Global Pulse operates at the intersection of data science, technology, and development to generate insights that inform evidence-based policy-making. The initiative originated in response to the recognition that traditional methods of data collection and analysis were insufficient to address the rapidly evolving challenges faced by the international community.

The core mandate of UN Global Pulse revolves around leveraging emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data analytics, to unlock real-time, actionable insights. By doing so, Global Pulse aims to enhance the UN system's ability to respond effectively to global crises, accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and address complex socio-economic challenges. Over the years, UN Global Pulse has pioneered innovative approaches to data analysis, experimentation, and collaboration. The initiative has actively engaged with governments, the private sector, academia, and civil society to build a network of Pulse Labs worldwide. These labs serve as localized hubs, exploring how data innovation can contribute to more effective and targeted development interventions at the country level.

The initiative to transition Pulse Lab Jakarta (PLJ) into the UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific Hub marks a pivotal phase for the UN Global Pulse in the Asia Pacific region. Shifting from country-level activities, the Regional Hub will now assume a broader regional role, focusing on convening stakeholders, sharing information, knowledge management, advocacy, and standard-setting. UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific aims to enhance efficiency in digital innovation efforts, contribute to policy-making, and address issues of exclusion and bias. 

The project is activated through a grant from the UN Foundation and aims at leveraging big data and artificial intelligence to achieve Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the Asia-Pacific region. The expanded scope includes emphasizing successful scaling, scanning regional gaps and challenges, and fostering broader innovation capabilities. The project design aligns with UN Global Pulse Core Functions, encompassing digital innovation programs, strategic foresight, and support for inclusive digital innovation policies. 

The project's theory of change outlines three impact channels: Innovation Solutions, Innovation Services & Capability Building, and Advocacy & Thought Leadership. These channels collectively aim to accelerate delivery, induce policy transformations, and generate social impact across the Asia-Pacific region. The project's programmatic considerations include stakeholder and communication management, partnership engagement, sustainable results management, gender mainstreaming, capacity building, and risk management.

The governance mechanism involves a Regional Steering Committee comprising the Government of Indonesia, multilateral, and philanthropic donors, responsible for providing strategic direction, advocacy, and overseeing program performance. The project team structure is designed for flexibility and efficiency, leveraging UNOPS support services and recruiting specialists to deliver on program objectives. 

UNOPS and UNGP-AP

The UNOPS team managing the UNGP-AP project brings its extensive expertise in project management, procurement, and operational support to ensure the successful establishment and functioning of the Regional Hub. UNOPS, known for its commitment to excellence in project delivery and adherence to the highest standards of transparency, efficiency, and accountability, will have to play a crucial role in overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Asia-Pacific initiative.

UNOPS will provide comprehensive support in the areas of fund management, administration, human resource management, procurement, and legal arrangements for strategic partnerships, including data partnerships and technical collaborations. Leveraging its vast experience in managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects, UNOPS will have to facilitate the smooth transition of Pulse Lab Jakarta into the UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific Hub.

In addition to operational support, UNOPS will contribute to risk management, ensuring that the project adheres to UNOPS risk management strategy and engages in continuous evaluation and mitigation of potential challenges. The organization's commitment to sustainability will be integral to the project's success, with a focus on mainstreaming gender considerations, promoting diversity, and addressing climate impacts throughout the implementation.

projects.name: 1.1.3.18 - Support HIV prevention services among populations that are most at risk, particularly female sex workers through strengthening implementation and integration the HIV prevention models
projects.description:
The UNFPA Programme would support intervention packages which include provision of HIV prevention commodities, access to ARV treatment and SRH services for female sex workers. Similar interventions are contemplated for the partner of key population and partner of people living with HIV (PLHIV) under the Partner Notification programme in government prioritized districts. In addition, the work will be delivered by engaging community-based organisations (CBOs) of female sex workers and PLHIV network as effective partners in HIV prevention efforts. It is in line with both capacity assessments of what is required to effectively implement the Global Fund grant and the division of labor among UNAIDS co-sponsoring agencies, UNFPA will support policy and programmes to strengthen HIV prevention and the link to SRH among most at risk populations, particularly female sex workers by:
●	Support to development of national policy and operational guidance for comprehensive and evidence based sex work interventions including access to SRH for sex workers;
●	Provide technical assistance for capacity building to (i) national counterparts on evidence for scaling-up effective HIV and SRH services for sex workers and inclusion in national policy and resources allocations, and (ii) civil society partners involved in programme implementation to support empowerment of sex worker networks and networking among them to participate in and meaningfully contribute to policy processes and/or programming; and
●	Support to implement a package of services in the government prioritized districts, including education and awareness, condom programming, outreach and drop-in centers, through which sex worker friendly HIV and SRH services can be provided and/or effective referrals made. Partnerships with law enforcement and other district level stakeholders such as the medical officer for sexually transmitted diseases, relevant non-governmental organizations and networks of sex workers to ensure a supportive environment for implementation of these programmes will be supported. Technical assistance will be provided to build skills of service providers in the mainstream health service to provide HIV and SRH services that are acceptable and accessible by sex workers.

It will be achieved through:
●	Advocacy dialogue with national and sub-national government to strengthen HIV policies related to prevention and treatment;
●	Development of national costed implementation Plan on STIs; and
●	Technical assistance, training and mentorship to strengthen Ministry of Health (MOH), Community Based Organizations (CBOs) leadership and capacity to implement innovative community-based service delivery, data collection and reporting

projects.name: 3.1.2.13 - 01000330 PIP Advancing Indonesia’s NDC targets in the energy sector (JSB NDC)
projects.description:
Indonesia has committed to reaching Net Zero Emission (NZE) by 2060 or earlier. Furthermore, Indonesia has increased by 14 percent its energy sector target of emission reduction by 2030 under the Enhanced NDC’s unconditional measures through increase in portion of renewable energy, reducing the use of fossil fuels, using electric vehicles in the transport sector, and implementing innovative climate technologies. However, the clear alignment between NZE and NDC targets and strategy of implementation to achieve higher emission reduction in the energy sector is lacking. Furthermore, Indonesia has also launched climate financing mechanisms like Energy Transition Mechanism (ETM) Country Platform, and Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing. Nevertheless, there is unclarity on how these financing mechanisms will be implemented and how the planned domestic carbon market can provide incentive for energy transition activities, particularly those are driven by the private sectors. For the private enterprises in the energy sector, technical assistance, investment, and technology facilitation are needed to advance the mitigation actions and commit to carbon neutrality within its production chains. 

To address these problems, the project is aimed to support Government of Indonesia in advancing NDC’s emissions reduction target in the energy sector through three Component Activities, namely: Support for the development of net-zero pathways for private companies (Component 1); Development of policy recommendation to increase energy sector targets in the NDC (Component 2); and Provide support to the Indonesia Environment Fund (IEF) to operate as a carbon credit standby buyer (Component 3). The project is expected to result in 50 studies of mitigation action from 50 companies committing to the net zero emission; 200 government officers and 150 non-party stakeholders will benefit from re-assessment of the energy sector policy to enhance emission reduction target, 70 mitigation actions validated or verified for issuance of Indonesia carbon certificate; and 6 carbon transactions take place in domestic market.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.2 - Government and private sector have increased capacity to develop policy options and access to financing for renewable energy and energy efficiency towards reducing GHG emission

projects.name: 4.1.3.25 - Advancing Development and Climate Action through Innovation in Indonesia and the Pacific Region
projects.description:
The establishment of the United Nations Global Pulse Asia Pacific Hub (UN Global Pulse AP) in 2023 resulted from a decade of successful collaboration between the Government of Indonesia, the Government of Australia, and the United Nations (UN). The hub was launched to scale the impact of innovations, translate innovation capabilities into policies, and leverage Indonesiaʼs expertise and lessons to accelerate the sustainable development agenda in the IndoPacific region. This project builds on these learnings and successful models, proposing the expansion of innovative solutions to address climate change and support the Government of Indonesiaʼs emerging priorities.
This project, outlines the programmatic activities of UN Global Pulse AP in Indonesia and the Pacific region for 2024-2026. In Indonesia, the hub will address key priorities for the Government of Indonesia by utilizing the full potential of data, AI, strategic foresight, behavioral science, and innovation scaling capabilities. This aligns with the governmentʼs ongoing commitment to leverage these tools for enhanced planning, decision-making, and policy development. In the Pacific region, the project will scale the Sea Level Rise (SLR) adaptation model, first piloted in Indonesia in 2024, to support adaptation strategies. With a new government taking office in October 2024, the "Asta Cita" vision—focused on economic growth, energy independence, and social welfare—will guide Indonesia toward "Golden Indonesia 2045." A key initiative, the Nutritious Meals Program, also launching in October 2024, aims to combat child malnutrition, stunting, and poverty by providing free nutritious meals to 82.9 million schoolchildren nationwide. To support this initiative, a Decision Support System (DSS) will be developed, integrating both official and non-conventional data for more effective decision-making. The possible use of strategic foresight, behavioral science, and scenario planning will ensure the program remains adaptive, enhancing health and educational outcomes while promoting economic development.
Rising sea levels pose a critical threat to Pacific Island nations, where coastal erosion, flooding, and saltwater intrusion jeopardize communities, livelihoods, and ecosystems. By replicating the Indonesian SLR model, the project will help Pacific nations enhance their resilience through data analytics and visualization, informing policy decisions and guiding targeted interventions in vulnerable areas. This data-driven solution effectively identifies areas at risk from rising sea levels and will complement existing resources while attracting new partners and investments, fostering innovation and sustainable development in the Pacific, thereby accelerating progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
The Indonesia-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership for 2020-2024 emphasizes strengthening economic and development cooperation, with a focus on evidence-based policies to reduce poverty and address inequality in Indonesia. This aligns closely with the Nutritious Meals Program, which uses data analytics to combat child malnutrition and stunting. The partnership also contributes to Indo-Pacific stability by supporting programs that advance the ASEAN Outlook, with a particular emphasis on climate resilience in the Pacific. Furthermore, trilateral cooperation between Indonesia, Australia, and Pacific Island nations fosters collaboration on climate resilience, which is a key focus of UN Global Pulse AP Hubʼs initiatives.

projects.name: 2.1.1.6 - 00127474 Enhancing Readiness for the Transition to Electric Vehicles in Indonesia (ENTREV)
projects.description:
Indonesia faces a significant increase in fossil fuel-powered land transportation, leading to increase in the greenhouse gases (GHGs) emissions under the energy sector, and local environmental issues like air pollution and noise pollution. With total number of motorcycle and cars of 150 million (2022), transportation is the second highest contributor to the greenhouse gases emission in the energy sector after power generation. Issuance of the Presidential Regulation No 55/2019 on Acceleration of Battery-Based Electric Vehicles (BEVs) supports the development of electric vehicles (EVs) as part of an overall transition from a fossil fuel-based transport sector to a cleaner transport sector. However, Indonesia's market diffusion of BEVs is still in the infant stage, and the EV ecosystems need to be strengthened. 

The EV ecosystems encompass policies, charging infrastructure, transport operators, EV technology providers, and EV users. ENTREV project aims to support the Government of Indonesia and key stakeholders in the BEV ecosystem for policy, institutional, technical & socio-environmental compliance readiness to transition towards electric mobility and to demonstrate innovative business models for the market adoption of two and four wheelers BEVs. 

The objective will be achieved through three (3) project component activities, namely: (1) Development of institutional framework and strategy for BEVs industry and charging infrastructure to enhance national market uptake; (2) Demonstration of early BEVs market development through pilot activities on BEV ecosystem development and facilitation of public-private investment in 4- wheeler charging stations (including one unit with solar-PV as source of electricity) and battery swap stations for 2- wheelers in DKI Jakarta, West-Java and Bali Provinces; and (3) Development of BEV knowledge products, capacity building, two-wheelers conversion technology to EV, and environmental standards for EV-battery management. By the end of four years, ENTREV project is expected to result in lifetime direct GHGs emission reduction of 473,800 tCO2 from the demonstration activities and the number of utilized BEVs; and indirect emission reduction of 6.1 million tCO2 ends from continue utilization and increase number of BEVs in 10 years after the project ends.

The project has been contributing to the following: 
1.	Development of the  Roadmap for BSS (SPBKLU) and 2-wheeler EVCS (SPKLU) Projection at the national level. This initiative aims to identify strategic locations for battery swap stations, ensuring widespread and accessible infrastructure for two-wheeler BEVs. Up to Q4 2025, the project has finalized the BSS and EVCS 2-wheeler projection for the year 2025-2030, and the spatial analysis for the projection result as well. 
2.	Developing the Single Gateway mobile apps (https://ngembangin.esdm.go.id/singgat-api/singgat-mobile.apk). This is a part of the Single Gateway website that has been developed (https://gatrik.esdm.go.id/singgat/ ).
3.	Developed a geospatial map for EVCS and Wilayah Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik (Wilus). The map is developed to monitor the implementation of Kepmen ESDM Nomor 24 Tahun 2025 by reviewing the spread of EVCS and Wilayah Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik (Wilus) location (https://www.cakrawala.cloud/)
4.	Developed studies on effectiveness of SPKLU connector type and 2 wheelers EV infrastructure (SPKLU 2 wheelers) standard. 
5.	Promoted Ease of Administration Process for Motorcycle Conversion Registration, aligned with Presidential Decree No. 79, 2023 (amending No. 55, 2019) on the Acceleration of the Battery Electric Vehicle Program for Road Transportation, and the Ministry of Transportation Regulation No. 15, 2022 regarding the conversion of combustion engine motorcycles to battery-based electric vehicles, by developing the application system (https://bit.ly/aplikasi_SUT-SRUT). 
6.	Collaborating with local governments (i.e. Bali, DKI Jakarta, and West Java), BSS and EVCS providers, and private sectors (i.e local companies/BUMD, land owner, etc.) in developing/install: 4 EVCS in West Java; 9 EVCS in DKI Jakarta; 5 BSS/Direct Charging in Bali through direct investment by the project and 15 BSS in Bali through co-financing with the private sectors (i.e. BSS providers, local government, and local company)

8.	Developing a virtual clearinghouse integrated within the Single Gateway platform. 
9.	Boosting BEV adoption by promoting BEV use through a collaboration with a Youth Organization (i.e SRE). This activity aims to invite 100 students to switch from their Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles to BEV. This one-year program aims to foster early adoption of electric vehicles among young people.

projects.name: 2.1.6.10 - Improving workers' skills and responsible business conduct (RBC) for transition (METI)
projects.description:
Decent work, poverty eradication and environmental sustainability are three of the defining challenges of the twenty-first century. Society must be inclusive, providing opportunities for decent work for all, reducing inequalities and effectively eliminating poverty. Today, the world is experiencing a phase of substantial changes - digital transformation due to the acceleration of technological advancement and implementation, and just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies for all. Accordingly, entire sectors are accommodating the structural transformations, rendering several human-performed occupations redundant. In the near future, these positions may be eliminated entirely. At the same time, other jobs are experiencing a rapid increase in demand, and some occupations are revising the skill sets they traditionally require.
The ILO will focus on three main objectives to ensuring workers' skills and RBC in this transition areas, i.e.: 1) to enhance skills, productivity and responsiveness to structural transformation and just transition; 2) to promote responsible business conduct and respect for the principle of international labour standards in harmony with the country’s development priorities; and 3) to promote an enabling environment in policy and practice to increase trade and investment into more value-added jobs and transition.

projects.name: 2.1.6.6 - Promoting Economic Empowerment of Women in Indonesia (WeEmpower Asia)
projects.description:
The overall objective of the action is to support sustainable, inclusive, and equitable economic growth by promoting economic participation and empowerment of women in Asia and EU countries. It aims to enhance the capacity of private sector companies to implement the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs)2 by promoting decent work opportunities for women and integrating a gender perspective in the business environment and practices. The action focuses on the role that the private sector can play in support of women’s economic empowerment in partnership with the public sector and networks of women’s entrepreneurs, women-led groups and associations. 
The proposed action will deliver the following three key results: (i) women’s networks, public institutions and the private sector in the EU and in Asia share expertise and knowledge to advance an enabling business environment for women’s economic empowerment; (ii) more private sector companies implement the WEPs, including gender-sensitive business culture and practices in the EU and Asia region; and (iii) women-led business and entrepreneurs have increased capacity to engage with governments and private sector companies in policies and dialogues for the advancement of women’s economic empowerment.  
The action is fully aligned to the objectives of the EU Partnership Instrument. The overarching implementation strategy of this action is South-South and Triangular Cooperation3 The proposed action intends to promote EU and international shared principles and values as well as to support economic, societal and social resilience in the EU by cooperating with selected Asian countries on the promotion of fair and equal competition based on international social standards. The immediate beneficiaries of this action include the private sector companies, women-led groups/business associations, governments, and public-sector institutions. The ultimate beneficiaries of this action include women's workers and entrepreneurs in the Asian region and EU. The action will specifically contribute to the new transformative Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which aims to reduce poverty (Goal 1) and inequalities (Goal 10), to achieve gender equality (Goal 5) and to promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all (Goal 8), and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development (SDG 17).

The project will deliver research and analysis, technical assistance, and policy recommendations on how to best implement online dispute resolution for consumers.

It will also build capacities of government officials on policy and technological aspects of online dispute resolution for consumers.

- Providing an updated picture of current consumer online dispute resolution systems globally, identifying best practices and lessons learnt. 
- Defining technical and infrastructure requirements of partner countries to develop ODR systems, including new technologies like block chain and AI.
- Building capacities in national consumer protection agencies, consumer groups and business associations on consumer ODR.
- Building consensus among partners on the modalities for delivering ODR and potential cost/efficiency improvement on trade among partner countries.

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 - Supporting Jakarta's transition to e-mobility
projects.description:
As the capital and largest city of Indonesia, Jakarta is facing a range of urban transport challenges including severe traffic congestion, air pollution, and high fuel consumption. To address these problems, the Government of Jakarta has made investments in its public transport system, including  a Bus Rapid Transit System with 13 trunk routes with a total ridership per day reaching 0.8 million.  Jakarta also has 2 Mass Rapid Transit lines with expansion underway. Efforts are already ongoing to connect inter-city and intra-city rail and integrate to the existing comprehensive bus system which will be significant to make urban transport more environment friendly. 

Though the increasing volume and quality of public transport can alleviate the city’s air pollutant and GHG emissions problems to a certain extent, a faster transition to electric mobility is required to meet its growing emissions from the transport sector. Air pollution is one of the key challenges along with congestion in the city. On bad days, Jakarta can find itself top of the list of the most polluted cities in the world. Further, the City of Jakarta contributes about 15% of GHG emissions of Indonesia, of which the Transport sector is a significant contributor. Thus, there is urgent need to decarbonize the transport sector.

Hence, the objective of this Technical Assistance is to support the Government of Jakarta, and the TransJakarta, a parastatal bus operator, in mainstreaming e-mobility in Indonesia, and particularly the deployment of electric buses in Jakarta.

Business and Human Rights in Asia: Enabling Sustainable Economic Growth through the Respect, Protect and Remedy Framework (B+HR Asia) is a joint action of the European Union (EU) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The action promotes and facilitates the implementation of the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), and in the process, contributes to stronger human rights conditions, inclusive economic growth, and environmental sustainability.  

UNDP B+HR Indonesia Project has contributed in creating an enabling environment to foster respect and protection of human rights within business operations through technical assistance provided to the Government of Indonesia (GoI) in establishing the National Taskforce on Business and Human Rights and subsequently supporting the National Taskforce to formulate the National Strategy on Business and Human Rights. The National Taskforce is the first formal mechanism created by the Government of Indonesia to formulate the policy on Business and Human Rights. The National Strategy will serve as the primary guidance for government and businesses in promoting responsible business conduct.  

 

In parallel with this policy development initiative, the B+HR Project has supported national and subnational government officials, businesses, association and civil society organizations to gain common understanding on responsible business conduct within the framework of Protect, Respect and Remedy of the UNGPs through awareness-raising and capacity building measures including series of public consultations, high-level dialogues, and training on business and human rights agenda and initiatives with the support of the European Union (EU).  

Immediate impacts resulted from the project interventions are including a strengthened commitment of GoI to implement UNGPs through their initiative to legitimize the National Strategy under a Presidential Decree.  

Building on these achievements, further awareness-raising and capacity building for key stakeholders including government, businesses (private, state-owned and SMEs), media and youth on BHR agenda as well as its linkages with environmental impacts are needed.

projects.description:
WFP partnered with the Government to enhance understanding on anticipatory action and assess the feasibility for its implementation in Indonesia. 
In partnership with the Ministry of Social Affairs, WFP assessed the local climate hazard risk profile and existing early warning and response mechanisms through a scoping exercise conducted in five provinces across Indonesia. These assessments have included discussions with local communities on how they address and respond to weather extremes and climate shocks. The results of this scoping exercise will inform WFP’s contribution to implementing anticipatory action. 

Further contributing to a strengthened common understanding on anticipatory action, WFP facilitated the participation of the Meteorological, Climatological and Geophysical Agency in the 6th Asia Pacific Dialogue Platform on Anticipatory Action in Bangkok, Thailand. The Agency gained additional knowledge on anticipatory action and shared progress and good practices from Indonesia, particularly on impact-based forecasting. Engagement at this regional event contributed to strengthened dialogue with the Coordinating Ministry of Human Development and Cultural Affairs on anticipatory action, along with other partners within the Risk-Informed Early Action Partnership (REAP). Such engagement will continue in 2023 in the form of enhanced policy dialogue on anticipatory action.

projects.description:
In 2018, severe natural disasters struck two provinces in Indonesia: a 7.0 magnitude earthquake in West Nusa Tenggara (NTB) on 5 August and, less than 8 weeks later - on 28th September - a 7.4 magnitude earthquake, followed by a tsunami and a rare phenomenon known as ‘soil liquefaction’, in Central Sulawesi. Beyond the immediate humanitarian and relief assistance, UNDP had initiated engagements with national and local governments and international partners in support of Central Sulawesi and NTB’s recovery efforts through The Sulawesi / Lombok Programme for Earthquake and Tsunami Infrastructure Reconstruction Assistance (PETRA) to ensure a smooth transition from the immediate response to longer-term recovery.
Despite all 54 completely built infrastructures that have been handed over to the local governments of NTB and Central Sulawesi provinces, the last batch that consisted of 19 (out of 54) have just been handed over to the local government of Central Sulawesi Province in mid of June 2024. Consequently, those 19 infrastructures still require support during their 12-month defect liability period (DLP) as PETRA Project ended its operation on 30 June 2024.
This PIP is to cover any activities incurred due to the DLP of those 19 infrastructures, yet not limited to the monitoring of DLP merely, as it will serve as an instrument for UNDP to identify potential initiatives related to resilience building in Central Sulawesi Province beyond the interventions already delivered by PETRA Project.

projects.name: Strengthening Resilience against Violent Extremism in Asia (STRIVE Asia)
projects.description:
The "Strengthening Resilience against Violent Extremism in Asia (STRIVE Asia)" project, a collaboration between the European Union and three UN agencies (UNODC, UNOCT, and UNDP), with UNODC as the lead agency in Southeast Asia, aims to enhance the partnership between law enforcement, civil society, and local communities to effectively and collaboratively prevent violent extremism. In Indonesia, the project identified three key thematic areas for intervention: strengthening Early Warning and Early Response (EWER), enhancing law enforcement capacity in community engagement, and promoting strategic communication for Prevention and Countering Violent Extremism.
In collaboration with the Jakarta Centre for Law Enforcement Cooperation (JCLEC), UNODC successfully capacitated and equipped 88 law enforcement officers from various parts of Indonesia with in-depth knowledge of the concept of violent extremism and the domestic and regional landscapes relevant to Indonesia’s counterterrorism and P/CVE legal frameworks. They were trained in community policing skills necessary for mobilizing community members, including women and youth, to understand the drivers of violent extremism and its early indicators, and to respond collaboratively and in a timely manner. Additionally, participants were equipped with pedagogical skills to ensure their ability to further impart expertise, knowledge, and skills to their law enforcement colleagues. 
In terms of EWER, UNODC and the Institute for International Peace Building (IIPB), or Yayasan Prasasti Perdamaian (YPP), convened a Multisectoral Consultation on Developing EWER in Central Java in Surakarta, Indonesia. Thirty participants from local government, law enforcement, and civil society discussed relevant legal frameworks and identified gaps, emphasizing the need for guidelines on development and capacity-building.
On the strategic communication front, the “Multisectoral Consultation on Strategic Communication for P/CVE” in East Java was held and attended by 30 government and civil society participants. Discussions highlighted the need for enhanced understanding of violent extremism threats, improved media literacy, and government capacity to counter online radicalization. Recommendations include developing guidelines for effective counternarratives and capacity building efforts. Subsequently, twenty Indonesian practitioners participated in a regional workshop in Bali, where they honed their skills and collaborated with peers from Malaysia and the Philippines to tailor communication strategies to various P/CVE efforts.
Parallel focus group discussions resulted in a research study on government and civil society partnerships in P/CVE in Indonesia, the findings of which were shared during a Regional Dialogue.

projects.description:
Enhance Indonesia’s technical capacity in analyzing the medium-term economic, social and environmental impacts of national policy priorities, through a newly developed macroeconomic model that integrates sustainable development. 
ESCAP will support Indonesia in the development of an Integrated National Financing Frameworks (INFF) to use existing financial resources in a more efficient and targeted manner and to raise additional resources to implement national development plans and finance the SDGs. It will bring together implementing entities’ existing SDG financing capacity and policy support to address capacity gaps identified in one or more of the four INFF building blocks (assessment and diagnostics, financing strategy, monitoring and review mechanisms, governance arrangements). ESCAP will support INFF-related assessments, offer capacity building and policy recommendations on topics such as financing needs and landscape, policies for public and private finance, monitoring for results, and institutional mechanisms. There will be an emphasis on synergizing with other ongoing and planned initiatives on financing for development, particularly related to ESCAP’s work on green bonds in Indonesia, and on peer learning from other countries, including through region-wide capacity development events.
ESCAP's will promote the utilization of green and SDG linked bonds as an instrument to support post COVID-19 recovery and the achievement of the 2030 Agenda. This initiative includes the development of a regional roadmap on green and SDG-linked bonds. Country level deep dive studies and national workshops will be undertaken this year, along with technical support for the issuance and listing of green and SDG linked bonds in the EU market.

projects.name: 3.1.2.10 - 00106637 UN Partnership for Action on Inclusive Green Economy (PAGE)
projects.description:
This project is the UNDP component of the multi-agency the Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) initiative. Since the start of its activities in 2013, PAGE has evolved from a small, coordinated effort  involving five United Nations agencies into a growing partnership supported by eight funding partners. UN PAGE brings together the expertise of ILO, UNDP, UNEP, UNIDO and UNITAR who work jointly in supporting countries to reframe macroeconomic and sectoral policies around sustainability. To date, PAGE has been active in 20 partner countries, and inspired action in a further 90 countries. In the decade 2020-2030, UN PAGE plans to build on this momentum by expanding and deepening its engagement with 10 additional countries and with regional organizations.

With the demand for the project continuing to grow, the UNDP project under PAGE has been extended for a period of four additional years from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2024. The substantive outputs remain unchanged. Management arrangements commensurate with the needs of the programme will be put in place, including recruitment of professional project staff(s). Additional funds received will cover the expanded work under the existing outputs.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.2 - Government and private sector have increased capacity to develop policy options and access to financing for renewable energy and energy efficiency towards reducing GHG emission
